technology_name: Nanocomposite Beads for Efficient Nitrate Removal: Ternary Nanocomposite Technology
institution: KSCSTE- Centre for Water Resources Development and Management (CWRDM)
problem_solved: Nitrate contamination in drinking water exceeding the safe permissible limit of 10 mg/L, causing serious health risks.
description: A cost-effective, sustainable ternary nanocomposite technology using Fe₃O₄@chitosan beads coated with Ag-doped TiO₂. The system combines the high adsorption capacity of magnetite (Fe₃O₄), the binding and biodegradable matrix of chitosan, and the advanced photocatalytic action of titanium dioxide (TiO₂). Silver (Ag) doping enhances the composite's visible light activity, enabling efficient solar-powered nitrate reduction via co-precipitation and sol-gel synthesis crosslinked with glutaraldehyde.
applications:
• Point-of-use (POU) domestic water purification systems and consumer filters

• Decentralized groundwater remediation schemes in high-fertilizer agricultural zones

• Large-scale industrial effluent treatment setups for nitrate-heavy manufacturing discharges

• Commercial production of functionalized photocatalytic water treatment media
secondary_sector: Advanced Materials & Chemical, Energy, Climate & Sustainability, Biotechnology & Life Sciences
